name: Trustworthy Distributed Learning
description:
This course explains the recently introduced federated learning setting and its multiple challenges. It will focus on data privacy, robustness against malicious client attacks, and the challenge of reducing the communication cost. The course will give an overview of the setting of decentralized learning and some of its challenges. A deep study of the recent machine learning algorithms and their fundamental properties, used to guarantee privacy, robustness, and communication efficiency, will be carried out.

More precisely, the course covers the following topics
- An introduction to distributed learning in its centralized, federated, and decentralized forms and the respective challenges arising.
- Basics of machine learning algorithms: gradient descent, stochastic gradient descent, linear and logistic regression, and basic neural network architecture
- Data privacy in distributed learning and the main tools to guarantee privacy, e.g., information-theoretic privacy through secret sharing and differential privacy.
- Schemes ensuring information-theoretic privacy in federated learning, their advantages and shortcomings.
- Combination of information-theoretic privacy and differential privacy in federated learning.
- Malicious client attacks in federated learning: known attacks and defense mechanisms.
- Designing robust federated learning schemes.
- Joint privacy and robustness in federated learning: challenges and schemes achieving them.
- Communication cost and model/gradient compression.
- A primer on decentralized learning and the challenges arising.
- An overview of schemes allowing robust and private decentralized learning and open problems for future research.
- A semester-long project requiring the students to implement state-of-the-art machine learning algorithms of their choice (fine-tuning LLMs, CNN, gradient descent ...) and making them privacy-preserving and or robust against attacks, and test the change in performance
prerequisites:
Knowledge of optimization, e.g., convex optimization, and machine learning
Knowledge of programming languages, e.g., Python, and basic experience with deep learning libraries such as PyTorch for a solid project
Basic knowledge of mathematics, e.g., linear algebra, calculus, and probability theory
The course "Channel Coding" is recommended
